card.name: Link words in history and ethnic-heritage text
card.fires_on: Small linking words, commas, or partway-through-place-name pieces in passages about history, peoples and heritage (Inuit, Ojibwa, Jacobite, Mesopotamia, Anglo-Saxon). They come just before a further place, people or era name.

modes.label: Links before people or places
modes.description: A comma or 'of' / 'for' / 'during' joining a list or phrase about nations, peoples or eras.
modes.example: 1 December 1720 – 31 January 1788) was the Jacobite claimant to the thrones of England<<,>> Scotland and Ireland. He is commonly known

modes.label: Inside historic place names
modes.description: Part of a long ancient place or heritage word such as Mesopotamia or African diasporic.
modes.example: the lowlands of southern Mesopot<<am>>ia and the Levant in the south

card.writes: It nudges the next word toward farmer, farm and rural or folk-culture terms.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in history and culture passages about peoples and old places.
